summary: The legal path length is capped at 3,000, and the scaling benchmark accepted a correct repeated single-replacement quadratic implementation. Matching output-size and scan lower bounds directly certify the current stack parser's optimality.

optimality.argument: A canonical absolute path may retain Theta(n) ordinary-name characters, so writing the required result takes Omega(n) time in the worst case. The current solution splits and classifies the input components once, performs amortized constant-time stack updates, and joins at most n retained characters once, giving O(n) time.

replacement_checks.evidence: For a path made of valid ordinary components with no redundant navigation, the canonical output has length proportional to the input and must be emitted in full.
Splitting visits the input once, each component causes at most one append or pop, and joining visits the retained components once.

The source-fidelity-verified examples cover repeated separators, parent navigation, root clamping, trailing separators, and period-only ordinary names; black-box real-test execution passed all five existing ordinary correctness checks.
